title: Search Tree K Largest Values
statement:
Return the largest values stored in a binary search tree, from largest to smaller values.

Contract
- `root` may be null and represents a binary search tree with distinct integer values.
- `k` is non-negative. Return at most `k` values.
- Values must appear in strictly decreasing order. If `k` is larger than the tree size, return every value.
- Do not mutate the tree.

Examples
`kLargest(tree(5, 3, 8, 2, 4, 7, 9), 3)` => `[9, 8, 7]`
`kLargest(tree(4), 5)` => `[4]`
`kLargest(null, 2)` => `[]`
hints: An inorder traversal of a search tree sees values in sorted order.
Visit right child, then the node, then left child to see values from largest to smallest.
Stop as soon as you have collected k values. Intended complexity: O(n) time in the worst case and O(h) stack space.
inputSyntax: Input: k followed by the tree in level order with null for missing children, for example: 3 [5, 3, 8, 2, 4, 7, 9]
